headline: Local Man Wins Hot Dog Eating Contest, Issues Statement of 'Immediate and Profound Regret'
summary: First-time competitor Gary Hendricks consumed 23 hot dogs in 10 minutes, spent remainder of weekend 'reconsidering everything.'
content:
Gary Hendricks, 41, achieved a personal milestone Saturday when he won the Founder's Day Hot Dog Eating Contest with a total of 23 frankfurters consumed in 10 minutes. He achieved another personal milestone approximately 15 minutes later when, according to witnesses, he "just sort of sat down on the curb and stared at the horizon for a really long time."

"I don't know what I expected," Hendricks told reporters Sunday, speaking from his living room couch where he had reportedly remained since Saturday evening. "I saw the sign-up sheet and I thought, 'I like hot dogs. I could do this.' And I could. I did. But at what cost?"

Hendricks, an accountant who describes himself as having "a normal relationship with food, historically," entered the contest on a whim after his children suggested he "needed a hobby." He now questions whether this was the hobby they had in mind.

"The human body can hold 23 hot dogs," Hendricks reflected. "I didn't know that before Saturday. I'm not sure I wanted to know that. That's information I now have to live with."

Second-place finisher Maria Santos, who consumed 19 hot dogs, appeared unbothered. "I do this every year," she said. "You get used to it. Also, I didn't go for 23. Twenty-three is a cry for help."

Hendricks received a trophy, a $50 gift card to the sponsoring restaurant, and what he described as "a new understanding of my own limitations, which apparently don't exist in the way I thought they did."

He has not yet decided whether he will defend his title next year. "I have 364 days to forget what this felt like," he said. "That might not be enough."
author: Marcus Webb, Features Writer
